title: Prym--Green Conjecture
body_md: For a general Prym curve $[C,\eta]\in\mathcal{R}_g$ of genus $g\geq6$, the homogeneous coordinate ring of the embedding defined by $L=K_C\otimes\eta$ has a natural minimal graded free resolution over $S$.
head: environment

label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
The Prym--Green conjecture holds in all even genera \mbox{$20\leq g\leq 30$}.
head: environment

label: lem:pg-section-ring
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pg-section-ring}
The section ring $R$ is a finite Cohen--Macaulay $S$-module of dimension $2$. Its graded canonical module is
\[
 M:=\omega_R=\operatorname{Ext}^{g-3}_S(R,S(-(g-1)))
 \cong\bigoplus_{q\geq0}H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes L^{\otimes q}).
\]
The sections $u,v$ form a regular sequence on both $R$ and $M$. For $N=R$ or $M$, putting $T=S/(u,v)$ gives
\[
 \operatorname{Tor}^S_i(N,k)_j\cong\operatorname{Tor}^T_i\bigl(N/(u,v)N,k\bigr)_j.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The pencil gives an exact sequence
\[
 0\longrightarrow L^{\otimes(q-2)}
 \xrightarrow{\,(-v,u)\,}
 (L^{\otimes(q-1)})^{\oplus2}
 \xrightarrow{\,(u,v)\,}L^{\otimes q}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Taking global sections shows that every relation between $u$ and $v$ in $R$ is a Koszul relation. In particular, $vb\in uR$ implies $b\in uR$. Since $u$ is a nonzerodivisor, $u,v$ is an $R$-regular sequence. For $q\geq3$, the vanishing of $H^1(C,L^{\otimes(q-2)})$ also gives
\[
 R_q=uR_{q-1}+vR_{q-1}.
\]
Thus $R$ is finite over $k[u,v]$, and hence over $S$. Its Hilbert function has linear growth, so its dimension is $2$. Regularity of $u,v$ then shows that it is Cohen--Macaulay.

For each integer $q$, graded local duality identifies $(\omega_R)_q$ with $H^2_{S_+}(R)_{-q}^{\vee}$ \cite[Section~3.6]{BH}. The \v Cech complex for $u,v$ gives $H^2_{S_+}(R)_a=H^1(C,L^{\otimes a})$, and consequently
\[
 (\omega_R)_q\cong H^1(C,L^{\otimes(-q)})^\vee
 \cong H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes L^{\otimes q}).
\]
These identifications respect multiplication by sections. The groups on the right vanish for $q<0$, since the corresponding line bundle is $\eta$ for $q=-1$ and has negative degree for $q\leq-2$. The canonical module is maximal Cohen--Macaulay, so $u,v$ is also regular on $M$.

Finally, tensoring a minimal graded free resolution of $N$ with $S/(u,v)$ preserves exactness because $u,v$ is $N$-regular. The resulting resolution is still minimal, proving the assertion about $\operatorname{Tor}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The preceding term in the degree-$m$ part of the Koszul complex is $\bigwedge^{m+1}V\otimes A_{-1}=0$. Hence
\[
 \ker\Phi_g=\operatorname{Tor}^T_m(A,k)_m\cong\operatorname{Tor}^S_m(M,k)_m.
\]
Since $R$ is a Cohen--Macaulay $S$-module of codimension $g-3$, graded local duality gives $\operatorname{Ext}^a_S(R,S(-(g-1)))=0$ for $a\ne g-3$ \cite[Theorem~3.6.19]{BH}. Dualizing a minimal graded free resolution of $R$ with respect to $S(-(g-1))$ and reversing the resulting complex therefore gives a minimal resolution of $M$. The claim follows by taking $i=j=m$ in
\[
 \dim\operatorname{Tor}^S_i(M,k)_j
 =\dim\operatorname{Tor}^S_{g-3-i}(R,k)_{g-1-j}.\qedhere
\]

label: lem:pg-equivalence
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put \mbox{$b_{p,q}=\dim K_{p,q}(C;L)$} and \mbox{$B=R/(u,v)R$}. The Hilbert series of $B$ is
\[
 H_B(t)=(1-t)^2H_R(t)=1+(g-3)t+gt^2.
\]
In particular \mbox{$B_1=V$} and \mbox{$B_q=0$} for \mbox{$q\geq3$}. By Artinian reduction, \mbox{$b_{p,q}=0$} for \mbox{$q\geq3$}. Also \mbox{$b_{p,0}=0$} for \mbox{$p>0$} because \mbox{$R_0=k$} and \mbox{$R_1=W$}. Comparing the coefficient of $t^{m-1}$ in
\[
 \sum_{p,q}(-1)^p b_{p,q}t^{p+q}
 =(1-t)^{g-3}\bigl(1+(g-3)t+gt^2\bigr)
\]
gives \mbox{$b_{m-2,1}=b_{m-3,2}$}, since that coefficient is zero. This proves the equivalence of (1) and (2).

Assume (1), and put \mbox{$p=m-3$}. Artinian reduction gives
\[
 K_{p,2}(C;L)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^T_p(B,k)_{p+2}.
\]
This group surjects onto
\[
 \bigwedge^pV\otimes\bigl(B_2/(V B_1)\bigr),
\]
because the outgoing Koszul differential is zero, while the incoming image lies in \mbox{$\bigwedge^pV\otimes V B_1$}. Since \mbox{$\bigwedge^pV\neq0$}, we obtain \mbox{$B_2=V B_1$}. Lifting generators from $B$ to $R$ now shows that $R$ is generated by $R_1$. Thus $L$ is normally generated. Since $L$ is ample and \mbox{$C=\operatorname{Proj} R$}, it also defines an embedding with homogeneous coordinate ring $R$.

Minimality and exactness imply that \mbox{$b_{i,1}=0$} forces \mbox{$b_{i+1,1}=0$} for \mbox{$i\geq1$} because a generator in the latter term could map only to the degree-\mbox{$i+1$} summands of the preceding term. Applying the same argument to the dual resolution shows that \mbox{$b_{i,2}=0$} implies \mbox{$b_{i-1,2}=0$} for \mbox{$1\leq i\leq g-3$}. Hence the two critical vanishings imply \mbox{$b_{p,1}=0$} for \mbox{$p\geq m-2$} and \mbox{$b_{p,2}=0$} for \mbox{$p\leq m-3$}. The resolution is therefore natural, and in fact pure. Conversely, naturality and \mbox{$b_{m-2,1}=b_{m-3,2}$} force both critical groups to vanish.

label: lem:pg-openness
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pg-openness}
Let $\pi\colon\mathcal C\to D$ be a proper flat family of geometrically integral nodal curves of arithmetic genus $g$ over a noetherian base, and let $\mathcal E$ be a line bundle that is nontrivial of order two on every geometric fiber. Set $\mathcal L=\omega_{\mathcal C/D}\otimes\mathcal E$. Then $\mathcal V_q=\pi_*\mathcal L^{\otimes q}$ is locally free and commutes with base change for $q\geq1$. The loci where $L_d$ is globally generated and where $K_{m-3,2}(C_d;L_d)=0$ are open in $D$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Cohomology and base change, together with the vanishing of $H^1(C_d,L_d^{\otimes q})$ for $q\geq1$, give the assertion about $\mathcal V_q$. For $p=m-3$, the complex of vector bundles
\[
 \bigwedge^{p+1}\mathcal V_1\otimes\mathcal V_1\longrightarrow
 \bigwedge^p\mathcal V_1\otimes\mathcal V_2\longrightarrow
 \bigwedge^{p-1}\mathcal V_1\otimes\mathcal V_3
\]
computes $K_{p,2}(C_d;L_d)$ on each fiber. Its middle homology has upper semicontinuous dimension, because the ranks of the differentials are lower semicontinuous. Thus $K_{p,2}=0$ is an open condition in such a family. Failure of global generation is the image of the support of $\operatorname{coker}(\pi^*\mathcal V_1\to\mathcal L)$, which is closed because $\pi$ is proper.

label: prop:specialization
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:specialization}
Suppose that $C_0,\eta_0$ are as above, that \mbox{$u,v\in H^0(C_0,L_0)$} have no common geometric zero, and that the resulting matrix $\Phi_g$ has full column rank. Then \mbox{$K_{m-3,2}(C;\omega_C\otimes\eta)=0$} for a general complex Prym curve \mbox{$[C,\eta]\in\mathcal{R}_g$}. In particular, the Prym--Green conjecture holds in genus $g$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first lift the nodal pair to characteristic zero and then smooth it, applying Lemma~\ref{lem:pg-openness} at each step.

Choose a discrete valuation ring $\Lambda$, obtained by localizing the ring of integers of a number field, with residue field $k$ and fraction field $F$. Lift the $2g$ marked points to sections of $\mathbb{P}^1_{\Lambda}$. They are pairwise disjoint, since their closed-fiber points are distinct. The pinching construction \cite[Theorem~5.4]{Fer} identifies these sections in the prescribed pairs. The resulting family has rational $g$-nodal fibers. It is flat over $\Lambda$ because its structure sheaf embeds in the pushforward of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1_\Lambda}$ and is therefore torsion-free over the DVR. A positive-degree line bundle on $\mathbb{P}^1_\Lambda$ descends after choosing identifications at the paired sections and is relatively ample, so the family is projective. Gluing the trivial line bundle with the same signs gives a line bundle of order two, nontrivial on both geometric fibers. Since $\Phi_g$ has full column rank, \eqref{eq:kernel} gives $K_{m-3,2}(C_0;L_0)=0$, and $L_0$ is globally generated by hypothesis. Both properties persist on the generic fiber. Extending scalars along an embedding $F\hookrightarrow\mathbb{C}$ therefore produces a complex nodal Prym pair $(C_1,\eta_1)$ with $K_{m-3,2}(C_1;\omega_{C_1}\otimes\eta_1)=0$.

We next smooth the complex nodal pair $(C_1,\eta_1)$. The stack of stable curves equipped with a line bundle of exact order two and a trivialization of its square is \'etale over $\overline{\mathcal M}_g$ \cite[Section~1.2.1, final paragraph, p.~608]{CF17}. Consequently, locally on a deformation space of $C_1$, the line bundle $\eta_1$ and its trivialization extend. Since stable curves are smoothable, we may choose a one-parameter smoothing of the pair $(C_1,\eta_1)$. After shrinking the base, all fibers are geometrically integral. The same openness argument then gives a smooth Prym curve with a globally generated paracanonical bundle and the required vanishing.

Finally, the same section of \cite{CF17} states that the smooth Prym stack is connected and \'etale over $\mathcal M_g$, hence smooth and irreducible. Thus both properties hold on a dense open subset of $\mathcal{R}_g$. For such a complex pair, choose a pencil in $H^0(C,L)$ with no common zero. Lemma~\ref{lem:pg-equivalence} then proves the Prym--Green conjecture.

label: lem:finite-field-specialization
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:finite-field-specialization}
Suppose $F(t)$ has zero kernel over $\mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)$. Then there are a finite extension $k/\mathbb{F}_p$ and $a\in k$ such that the points $P_j(a),Q_j(a)$ are pairwise distinct and the corresponding Prym curve admits sections $u_a,v_a$ with no common geometric zero for which $\Phi_g$ has zero kernel.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The moving marked points define a family of rational $g$-nodal curves $\pi\colon\mathcal C\to U$ over an open neighborhood $U$ of $0$ in $\mathbb A^1_{\mathbb{F}_p}$. To construct this family, remove the finitely many parameters at which two marked points coincide, and identify the corresponding sections in pairs. Use the same gluing signs to define the relative line bundle $\mathcal E$ of order two, and put $\mathcal L=\omega_{\mathcal C/U}\otimes\mathcal E$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:pg-openness}, the sheaves $\pi_*\mathcal L^{\otimes q}$ are locally free and commute with base change for $q\geq1$. After shrinking $U$ around $0$, lift the chosen sections $u(0),v(0)$ to sections $u,v$ of $\pi_*\mathcal L$. Their common-zero locus has closed image in $U$ because $\pi$ is proper. This image does not contain $0$, so we may shrink $U$ further to ensure that $u,v$ have no common geometric zero on any fiber.

By the reduction above and Lemma~\ref{lem:pg-matrix}, injectivity of $F(t)$ gives
\[
 K_{m-3,2}(C_{\mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)};L_{\mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)})=0.
\]
The Koszul complex commutes with the field extension $\mathbb{F}_p(t)\subset\mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)$. Faithful flatness therefore gives the same vanishing on the generic fiber over $U$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:pg-openness}, this vanishing holds on a nonempty open subset $U^\circ\subset U$. Choose a closed point of $U^\circ$. Its residue field $k$ is finite over $\mathbb{F}_p$, and its parameter value is an element $a\in k$. The marked points are distinct and the specialized pencil has no common geometric zero. Lemma~\ref{lem:pg-matrix} therefore gives $\ker\Phi_g=0$.

title: Remark
body_md: We remark that our program internally does not actually compute two-parameter families explicitly, but only one parameter families modulo $t^3$. However, it makes choices that produce data that are compatible with the $C_m$-action in the above sense. Below it will suffice to know only the above properties (1) and (2) of $F(t)$, which the program enforces, respectively checks. The analysis of this section shows that there exist such choices, but it should not be seen as a direct algorithmic description of the program.

label: prop:computational-result
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:computational-result}
For \mbox{$g\in\{22,26,30\}$} and the parameter values specified above, the matrix $\Phi_g$ is injective over $\mathbb{F}_p$. Moreover, for \mbox{$g\in\{20,24,28\}$} and the deformations specified above, the matrix $\Phi_g(t)$ is injective over $\mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For $g=22,26,30$, Proposition~\ref{prop:computational-result} supplies rational nodal Prym curves over finite fields for which $\Phi_g$ has full column rank. The pencils used in their construction have no common geometric zero by the checks in Section~\ref{sec:artinian}. For $g=20,24,28$, Proposition~\ref{prop:computational-result} gives injectivity of $\Phi_g(t)$ over $\mathbb{F}_p(\!(t)\!)$, equivalently of $F(t)$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-field-specialization} supplies finite-field Prym curves satisfying the same hypotheses. Proposition~\ref{prop:specialization} then proves the required vanishing for a general complex Prym curve in each of the six genera.
